html:
The Umatilla are a Sahaptin-speaking people of the Columbia Plateau in northeastern Oregon, along the Umatilla River and the Columbia River.

They lived from the salmon runs, roots such as camas, and game, moving between river villages and mountain camps with the seasons. They traded and married with their neighbours the Cayuse, the Walla Walla, the Yakama and the Nez Perce.

The Lewis and Clark Expedition passed through their land in 1805. In the 1840s the Oregon Trail brought migrants and disease. Under an 1855 treaty the Umatilla, Cayuse and Walla Walla were placed on one reservation near Pendleton, Oregon, and today form the Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla Indian Reservation.
sum: The Umatilla are a Sahaptin-speaking people of the Columbia Plateau in northeastern Oregon, along the Umatilla River and the Columbia River.
